title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 181 (Apportionment of relief or compensation obtained by such suits)

content.overview: Section 181 provides that whatever is obtained by way of relief or compensation in any such suit shall, as between the bailor and the bailee, be dealt with according to their respective interests.
content.glance: Relief or compensation obtained in a suit under Section 180 is, as between the bailor and the bailee, dealt with according to their respective interests.
content.study: Whatever is obtained by way of relief or compensation in any such suit shall, as between the bailor and the bailee, be dealt with according to their respective interests. Current-law framing: internal accounting between bailor and bailee of the fruits of the suit against the wrong-doer.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Whatever is obtained by way of relief or compensation in any such suit shall, as between the bailor and the bailee, be dealt with according to their respective interests.

examples.title: Apportionment of compensation
examples.body: Compensation recovered in a suit under Section 180 is apportioned between bailor and bailee according to their respective interests under Section 181.

hypotheticals.question: Compensation is recovered in a suit by the bailee against a wrong-doer. How is it dealt with between bailor and bailee?
hypotheticals.analysis: According to their respective interests, under Section 181.
